claims.text: Ophthalmopathy = treated jointly w ophthalmology and may need selenium, glucocorticoids, orbital radiation and surg.
claims.quote: Ophthalmopathy should be treated jointly by the endocrinologist and ophthalmologist and may require selenium, glucocorticoids, orbital radiation, and surgery

claims.text: Radioiodine can accelerate active ophthalmopathy and = contraindicated in that phase.
claims.quote: Radioiodine therapy may accelerate progression of ophthalmopathy when ophthalmopathy is active, and is thus contraindicated in this active phase.

claims.text: Infiltrative dermopathy (pretibial myxedema): topical glucocorticoids or glucocorticoid injections into the lesions may help.
claims.quote: In infiltrative dermopathy (in Graves disease), topical glucocorticoids or glucocorticoid injections into the lesions may decrease the dermopathy.

claims.text: Mild active GO treated w RAI: consider glucocorticoid coverage (⍉a strong contraindication), even w.o RF.
claims.quote: In the absence of any strong contraindication to GC use we suggest considering them for coverage of GD patients with mild active GO who are treated with RAI, even in the absence of risk factors
claims.locator: Ross DS, et al. 2016 American Thyroid Association Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Hyperthyroidism and Other Causes of Thyrotoxicosis. Thyroid 2016;26(10):1343-1421
